name: Pass Merge to Eliminate Repeated Global Memory Access
matchText: Pass Merge to Eliminate Repeated Global Memory Access: The same data or an unchanged pointer expression is loaded from or stored to GM repeatedly across passes, for example an intermediate written to a GM buffer in one pass and reloaded from the same buffer in a later pass, when the passes could be fused so the value stays on chip.
content:
Problem:
Repeated passes write an intermediate to global memory and reload it later, multiplying
GM loads, masks, loop control, and scalar reduction overhead.

Recommended changes:
- Fuse compatible passes into a single traversal so an intermediate produced by one part
  of the pass is consumed on chip instead of being written to GM and reloaded later.
- Accumulate the statistics used by a later stage (for example the sum-of-squares feeding
  a row-wise rsqrt normalization) in the same traversal that produces the intermediate.
- Keep the row tile on chip for the full pass so the final store happens only once.

Constraints:
- Check peak on-chip storage (UB) before eliminating a loop.
- Retain separate passes only when a true dependency forces a second traversal.
- Preserve mathematical equivalence, accumulation dtype, and required operation order.
